text:
Wyatt Johnston spent October getting chances and not much else. Now the goals are arriving: one in each of his last three games, including the one that cut Vegas's lead to 3-2 with 1:18 left on Tuesday, a puck that deflected straight to him at the back door. Jesse Granger called it a fortunate bounce, and maybe it was, but he was standing in the right place.

That's the whole story of his season. Six goals on 9.7 expected is the biggest gap between chances and goals on the Stars, and his own shot rate is up to 1.56 expected goals per 60 from 1.30 last season. Players who keep getting looks like that tend to score. He's also carrying the power play: 11 of his 19 points have come with the man advantage.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 93rd percentile for chances from the slot area last season, and Evolving-Hockey said the same thing we see now, chances that deserved more than his goals delivered. The caveat from Evolving-Hockey is defensive: opponents created more with him on the ice (bottom 12% of forwards).
